fixes.explanation: They ask, “Are you the Prophet?” and John answers, “No.” (John 1:21) That's one short word. It's the third thing in a row that John says he is not, after the Christ and Elijah.
The text says John does answer no. The visitors ask, “Are you the Prophet?” and he answers, “No.” (John 1:21) That's one more title he says he isn't, after the Christ and Elijah.
John replies “…in the words of Isaiah the prophet…” (John 1:23) A prophet is someone who speaks for God. So John doesn't describe himself with his own words. He uses the words of Isaiah.

No walls in this one, baker. The voice in the wilderness calls, “Make straight the way for the Lord.” (John 1:23) A crooked wall would bother me too, but that's not the call. The thing getting straightened is the way for the Lord.

Straight rows are lovely, and I line up my chocolate chips that way myself, but that's not the call. The voice says, “Make straight the way for the Lord.” (John 1:23) It's the Lord's way that gets straightened, not a field.
John says, “…among you stands One you do not know.” (John 1:26) He's speaking to the Pharisees, and he says this One is standing among them. Think about that. They don't know Him.
Beside Him isn't where John puts himself. He says he isn't worthy to untie the straps of this One's sandals. (John 1:27) If John isn't worthy of even that, then this One is not a servant like John.

John says, “…the reason I came baptizing with water was that He might be revealed to Israel.” (John 1:31) So John's baptizing has a purpose behind it. Revealed means made known, and that's what John says it was for.

John isn't told anything about oil. The One who sent him said the man he sees the Spirit rest on “…is He who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.” (John 1:33) Oil sounds fancy, I'll give it that, but it's not what he was told. The answer is the Holy Spirit.
John says, “I have seen and testified that this is the Son of God.” (John 1:34) He says he saw the sign with his own eyes. Then he testified about it.

New king is a fine title, but John never gives it to Jesus here. His testimony is, “I have seen and testified that this is the Son of God.” (John 1:34) Son of God is the title John gives. It's about who Jesus is, not about a throne.
